subtopic: Target Date Funds as 401(k) Default Investments
source_evidence: Some 401(k) plans use these funds as the default investment for plan participants who have not selected their investments under the plan.
question: Misconception: If a target date fund is the default investment in my 401(k), that means it is automatically the right choice for me.
answer: A default investment is used when a plan participant has not selected investments; being the default does not establish that the fund is right for every participant. The source advises considering carefully whether the fund is right for you.
